wizard.title: New job
wizard.tablesColumns: {tables, plural, one {# table} other {# tables}} · {columns, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}

type.title: What do you want to do?
type.description: Pick the kind of job. The next steps follow from it: a name, the connections, then what happens to each column.

dataSync.name: Copy and anonymize
dataSync.description: Real data, transformed column by column, written to a test database.

generate.name: Generate data
generate.description: Fully synthetic rows for a chosen destination, from the schema only.

aiGenerate.name: Generate with AI
aiGenerate.description: Synthetic rows written by a model, shaped by a table schema and your prompt.

piiDetection.name: Find personal data
piiDetection.description: A report of the sensitive columns in a database, without copying anything.

define.title: Name the job
define.description: A unique name, then when it should run.

schedule.title: When should it run?
schedule.description: Without a schedule, the job is paused and runs only when you trigger it; a default cron is stored.
schedule.onDemandHint: From the interface, the CLI or the API.

initiate.title: Once it is created
initiate.description: Start a single run right after the job is created, or keep it for later.
initiate.ariaLabel: Initiate a job run after creation

advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.runTimeoutDescription: The maximum length of time (in minutes) that a single job run is allowed to span before it times out. 0 means no overall timeout.
advanced.runTimeoutTables: A table has no limit of its own: it is stopped when it no longer makes progress. At this limit, the run stops the tables still being copied and puts the destination triggers back.
advanced.engineDescription: Transformation engine used to run this job. Default follows the deployment setting.
advanced.consistencyScopeDescription: Deterministic consistency (Athanor engine only): the same source value gets the same anonymized value everywhere in this scope. Beyond a single run, outputs stay linkable over time.

pii.startToCloseDescription: The maximum amount of time (in minutes) a single table detection may run before it times out. This timeout is applied per retry.
pii.scheduleToCloseTitle: Max PII Detection Timeout including retries
pii.scheduleToCloseDescription: The total time (in minutes) that a single table detection is allowed to run, including retries. 0 means no timeout.
pii.retryDescription: The maximum number of times a table detection may retry before giving up.  If not set or set to 0, it means unlimited retry attempts and the max table timeout including retries will be used to know when to stop.

sync.startToCloseDescription: The maximum amount of time (in minutes) a single table page synchronization may run before it times out. This may need tuning depending on your datasize and how well optimized the indices on the table. This is applied to every table page sync and generate. This timeout is applied per retry.
sync.scheduleToCloseDescription: The total time (in minutes) that a single table sync is allowed to run, including retries. 0 means no timeout.
sync.retryDescription: The maximum number of times a table sync may retry before giving up.  If not set or set to 0, it means unlimited retry attempts and the max table timeout including retries will be used to know when to stop.

schema.title: Which tables, and what becomes of each column?
schema.description: Check the tables to copy. Columns detected as personal start with an anonymizing transformer; review them, then adjust any column one by one.

subset.title: Reduce the volume?
subset.description: Filter a starting table with a WHERE clause; related tables follow through their keys. Leave every filter empty to copy everything.

unsupported.title: Heads up!
unsupported.description: Subsetting is not currently enabled for this connection type. You may proceed with the creation of this job while we continue to work on subsetting for this connection.

summary.filtered: {count, plural, one {# filtered table} other {# filtered tables}}

addDestinations.title: Add destinations
addDestinations.descriptionFrom: Where else should the anonymized data from {name} be written? Only connections compatible with the source are listed.
addDestinations.description: Where else should the anonymized data be written? Only connections compatible with the source are listed.
addDestinations.empty: No other connection can receive data from this source.

connect.title: Where should the generated data go?
connect.description: A connection gives the shape of the tables; the destination receives the synthetic rows. Both can be the same database.

schemaConnection.title: Table schema connection
schemaConnection.description: The connection whose tables give the shape of the data to generate. It can be the destination itself.

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: Where the generated rows are written.

schema.title: What should be generated?
schema.description: Pick the table to fill, how many rows, and the generator of each column.
schema.numRowsDescription: The number of rows to generate.

newJob.formErrors: Please fix form errors and try again.

connect.title: Which model, and where should its data go?
connect.description: An OpenAI-compatible connection writes the rows; a database connection gives the shape of the table and receives the result.

model.title: Model connection
model.description: An OpenAI-compatible API to generate data from.

connect.schemaConnectionDescription: The connection whose table gives the shape of the data to generate. It can be the destination itself.

schema.title: What should the model generate?
schema.description: Pick the table to fill, the model and its prompt. Sample a few rows before creating the job.
schema.modelDescription: The name of the model to use.
schema.promptDescription: Optionally provide a prompt to give further context to the model. This is highly recommended! The table schema will be appended to the end of this prompt automatically.
schema.batchSizeDescription: The batch size used when asking the model to generate records. Useful for large datasets or prompts that may exceed AI token limits. Smaller is generally better.

sampleTable.title: Synthetic data sample
sampleTable.description: A sample of synthetic data given the inputs above: the configured row count, up to 10 records.
sampleTable.empty: Click Sample to generate a preview of synthetic data.

connect.title: Which database should be scanned?
connect.description: The job reads column names and a sample of rows to find personal data. Nothing is copied.
connect.sourceDescription: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server connections can be scanned.

schema.title: How should the scan run?
schema.description: What to look for, how many rows to sample, and which tables to read. The analysis runs where your data is.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: The connection to use for the PII detection job.

userPrompt.title: User Prompt
userPrompt.description: Optionally input a prompt to guide the LLM part of the PII detection job.
userPrompt.placeholder: Do NOT classify the following columns as PII or personally identifiable information: id, created_at, updated_at

dataSampling.title: Data Sampling
dataSampling.description: Let the job read rows of each table. Up to 200 rows per table are read by the worker, inside your deployment, to recognise formats such as email addresses, IBANs or card numbers. When disabled, no row is read: only table names, column names and column types are used.

modelInput.title: What the model receives
modelInput.description: Choose what the language model is given about the sampled rows.
modelInput.profilesDescription: The language model receives the table name, the column names and types, and statistics computed from the sampled rows: counts, lengths, kinds of characters, formats. No value of your data is sent to the model.
modelInput.valuesDescription: In addition, the language model receives up to 5 distinct values of each column, each cut to 64 characters. These values leave the worker for the model endpoint configured on this deployment. Choose this only if that endpoint may receive this data, for example a model hosted inside your network.

dataSampling.noModel: With no model configured, nothing is sent anywhere: detection uses the rules only. Rules alone do not find personal data in a column with a neutral name, unless its values have a format the rules check, such as email addresses, IBANs, card numbers or password hashes.

incremental.title: Incremental Scans
incremental.description: Allow the job to incrementally detect PII for new or changed tables. This will only scan tables that have been added or updated since the last successful run. New table detection is dependent on the scan mode and patterns selected below.

scanMode.title: Table Scan Mode
scanMode.description: The mode to use for the table scan filter. This will determine what schemas and tables will be scanned for PII.

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description: The patterns to use for the table scan filter based on the mode selected. A combination of schemas and tables will be scanned based on the mode and selection.
